reader.title: Rumored lynching of Charles LaFour
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: The only report is a rumor that LaFour was "lynched by a mob" after killing a man; nothing confirms that any killing took place (A1).

A single item repeats an unconfirmed rumor that LaFour was lynched by a mob for killing a man, and the quoted paper says it had learned "nothing certain" (A1). No report confirms the death, the mob, or the circumstances.
One white-press item, a reprint from the Fond du Lac Commonwealth that calls the story a rumor; the Superior paper that reprinted it added no local confirmation (A1).

summary.text: The rumored lynching of Charles LaFour was an unconfirmed report, printed in Wisconsin in early January 1882, that a man known to the Fond du Lac police had killed a man at Superior City on Lake Superior and been lynched by a mob.
The story rested on a rumor that the Fond du Lac Commonwealth said it could not verify, and no confirming report appears in the coverage.
According to the Fond du Lac Commonwealth, a rumor reached that city that LaFour, "well-known in police circles here," had killed a man at Superior City and "was lynched by a mob."
The item did not name the man LaFour was said to have killed, give a date, describe the mob, or state the race of anyone involved.
The Commonwealth added that an effort had been made that day to learn the truth, but that "nothing certain has yet been learned."
No report of an inquest, arrest, correction or denial appears in the coverage, so whether LaFour was killed is not established.
The only surviving trace of the story is a reprint in the Superior Times of January 7, 1882, which ran the Commonwealth paragraph in its "From Our State Exchanges" column.

The Superior paper, published in the town where the lynching was said to have occurred, placed the item among notices of fires, thefts and a railroad extension and added no comment or local information of its own.
